items.summary: The First Dog on the Moon cartoon poses a question about Google's AI summary, suggesting it may damage the company's profits. The piece asks whether this development helps or hurts Google and implies that its own search has become less handy.
items.title: First Dog on the Moon questions whether Google search is still useful

items.summary: Shares of supermarket operator Sheng Siong fell over 9% to a one-year low after the group reported a marginal 1.9 per cent rise in third-quarter net profit, reaching S$44.6 million from S$43.7 million. Revenue rose 6.2 per cent to S$441.5 million. Management cited competition ahead of the RTS Link and rising labour costs as challenges. DBS analyst Chee Zheng Feng expects further earnings moderation in the fourth quarter.
items.title: Sheng Siong Shares Hit One-Year Low on Weak Outlook

items.summary: Gold rose as much as 0.7% toward nearly US$3,900 an ounce after a 3.7% drop the prior session and its worst October since 2008. Spot gold climbed 0.6% to US$3,899.39 in Singapore at 7.45am. Strategist Justin Lin of Global X ETFs cited dip buying but warned of precarious levels; Ole Sloth Hansen of Saxo Bank AS noted technical selling and vulnerability below US$3,886, with a recovery above US$4,000 needed for neutrality.
items.title: Gold Rebounds From One-Year Low on Dip Buying

items.summary: A five-month real-time facial recognition trial in Western Australia scanned 1,380,882 faces across 100 deployments, producing 122 arrests and nine incorrect alerts. WA police commissioner Col Blanch said no one was arrested over the false matches but that officers engaged each person. Civil Liberties Australia's Bill Rowlings criticised the error rate framing, arguing it should be measured against convictions while scans occurred without reasonable suspicion.
items.title: WA Facial Recognition Trial Yields 122 Arrests Amid Privacy Criticism

items.summary: The article argues that smart home technology should be chosen for return on investment rather than novelty, presenting five upgrades with genuine savings and three overengineered gadgets to skip. Smart thermostats like Nest and Ecobee use geofencing and motion sensors to ease HVAC automatically; households save around 10% on heating and 15% on cooling, plus utility rebates may apply. Water leak sensors can prevent damage from slow drips behind a washing machine or under a water heater, where the average residential claim costs more than $10,000.
items.title: Smart Home Devices That Save Money Versus Those Worth Skipping

items.summary: The author republished from Wonder Tools describes testing twelve AI agents to act proactively without prompts. Early favorites are Dots, Slashy, and Hark for calendar conflicts, email management, and design. Costs vary: some start free while ChatGPT's Pro plan is $100/month. The writer advises starting with one agent and checking ongoing costs before connecting accounts.
items.title: I auditioned 12 AI agents to be my chief of staff. Here’s how they compared

items.summary: VinEnergo has commissioned a rooftop solar system integrated with battery storage in the Vung Ang Economic Zone, Ha Tinh, Vietnam. It will supply clean electricity to VinFast’s vehicle plant, the VinES and VG battery facilities under its first Direct Power Purchase Agreement installation. Company estimates put first-year generation at about 39 million kWh, cutting emissions by more than 25,000 tonnes annually.
items.title: VinEnergo Commits Rooftop Solar And Storage To Vietnamese Factories

items.summary: HYXI presented solar and energy storage solutions across residential, commercial, industrial and utility-scale segments at Renewable Energy India (REI) Expo 2026 in Greater Noida from October 22 to 24. At Hall 15, Booth C279, the company displayed microinverters, string inverters and energy storage systems alongside its HYXI Cloud monitoring platform. Ashish Bisht, Country Manager of HYXI, said India offers significant opportunities for smart solar solutions as the company seeks to expand its presence in the Indian market.
items.title: HYXI Showcases Solar and Storage Solutions at REI Expo 2026

items.summary: Inside Climate News examines whether Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro will be judged harshly for his data center record as he considers a 2028 presidential run. Over about 20 months, Shapiro moved from fast-tracking hyper-scale data centers to an executive order slowing development. Republican opponent Stacy Garrity used the shift in attacks without electoral gain, while polls suggest it remains a lasting vulnerability: this July’s Quinnipiac poll showed Shapiro at 56 percent approval overall but underwater on AI data centers (24 percent approve, 34 percent disapprove). Emerson and Muhlenberg College polls later found growing public concern. Shapiro introduced GRID standards in February, which critics called not legally binding; he then removed data centers from the Fast Track program in August using words like “greedy” and “predatory.” His office declined to directly answer questions about his motives. Observers remain divided on whether his pivot is genuine or political.
items.title: Shapiro’s Data Center Flip Faces Political Test

items.summary: Boehm, Levchenko and Xiang model optimal tariffs with a time-to-build lag in firm creation. Protection raises future domestic firms but costs higher prices now. Without commitment to future tariffs, short-run price concerns preserve freer trade and derail manufacturing growth.
items.title: Time-Inconsistent Tariffs Undermine Manufacturing Renaissance in Model

items.summary: John Ternus will host his first Apple earnings call on Monday, with investors weighing whether a wave of new products can offset surging memory-chip costs. The company has shipped its first foldable phone, smart home hub and touch-screen laptops this fiscal quarter. Analysts expect profit growth to fall to its weakest in six quarters as holiday-quarter results approach.
items.title: Apple's new CEO Ternus faces first earnings test amid rising memory costs

items.summary: Connecticut launched LEAP in summer 2021, sending school personnel on home visits to chronically absent students across its 15 most disadvantaged districts. Brunner, Jiang and Ross estimate attendance rose about 4–5 percentage points while chronic absenteeism fell 13–15 points; effects held steady after correcting for selection.
items.title: Connecticut Home Visits Boost Attendance for Absent Students

items.summary: Reports indicate Apple is preparing updates for three iPad models, including the entry-level tablet, iPad Air and iPad Pro, with launches expected in the first half of 2027. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says Apple is now focusing on its remaining tablets after updating the iPad mini with an OLED display in October. The company has not confirmed these changes.
items.title: Apple reportedly plans iPad lineup refresh in first half of 2027

items.summary: Actor Ranbir Kapoor drew a playful comparison between Elon Musk's newly showcased flying Tesla Roadster and the Pushpaka Vimana from the Ramayana, saying India had invented a flying vehicle 5,000 years ago. He made the remark during a promotional interaction for Ramayana, scheduled to release on November 5.
items.title: Ranbir Kapoor Compares India's Ancient Flying Vehicle to Musk's Tesla Roadster

items.summary: Share markets steadied across Asia on Monday as investors awaited Apple earnings, hoping for relief from AI cash-burn worries while oil prices eased after talks continued between Iranian and Qatari mediators. Apple shares have climbed four months straight to unseat Nvidia as the world's most valuable listed company. Analysts expect quarterly EPS of $2 on revenue of $113 billion, up from $1.85 a year earlier. Optimism helped S&P 500 futures edge up 0.4 per cent and Nasdaq futures bounce 0.8 per cent after October's worst month since April 2025. Goldman Sachs analysts expect hyperscaler capex to almost double to $800 billion this year, rising to $1.2 trillion in 2027. Ben Snider wrote that earnings growth is strong but no longer accelerating.
items.title: Asian Shares Steady on Apple Earnings Hopes and Falling Oil

items.summary: The author, who describes themselves as not religious, examines why people feel grief and mourn the death of those believed to be heading to heaven. They note that mourning is sincere but question whether celebrating a departure toward heaven should instead bring happiness. The author suggests this tension reflects mood management: people construct portfolios mixing positive and negative emotions during stressful situations, adjusting their emotional balance as needed rather than staying consistent over time. This same pattern, the author argues, appears in debates about AI, where people hold both love and dislike for models to avoid a non-diversified emotional portfolio.
items.title: Author Questions Grief for Those Heading to Heaven

items.summary: Semafor reports that The Daily Caller, co-founded by Tucker Carlson in 2010 as the Republican Party’s answer to The New York Times, has shifted sharply against Donald Trump’s war in Iran and toward criticism of Israel. Publisher Neil Patel told Semafor he faced aggressive donor pressure over the turn, though he declined to detail financial costs. Editor-in-Chief Amber Duke said the Iran war marked a turning point for conservatives. Critics accuse the outlet of antisemitism; Fox host Mark Levin called it “Al Jazeera in Arabic.” Former staff worry about its drift toward the ‘groyper’ wing and damage to its talent pipeline.
items.title: Daily Caller turns against Trump and Israel

items.summary: A column profiles Katy Hoffman, a 33-year-old registered dietitian in Kansas City who gained attention by investigating billionaire Amy Griffin's memoir claims. Hoffman confronted Billy Bush at a wedding on Lanai and shared court documents and audio recordings online. Society figures reportedly listen to her posts without following them publicly. She describes herself as 'just a nosy lady' and credits the Griffin case with teaching her investigative journalism, though she feels intimidated by professional reporters now contacting her about her Patreon.
items.title: Kansas City dietitian becomes society sleuth behind Amy Griffin feud

items.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Sunday he had a good conversation with US President Donald Trump about the future of Canada-US trade, building on recent constructive discussions toward a mutually beneficial deal. Trump added his administration has the concept of an agreement benefiting farmers. The two leaders have exchanged messages as tariffs and talks continue amid uncertainty over timelines.
items.title: Carney and Trump Signal Progress on Canada-US Trade Deal

items.summary: US technology shares had their worst selloff in months last week as disappointing quarterly results raised doubts about whether heavy AI spending will pay off. Alphabet led the rout, with its stock falling 13% on October 29 after revenue of $127.6 billion missed expectations and earnings came in at $2.12 versus a forecast of $3.02. The pain spread to chipmakers, including Intel's 29% plunge on October 30, as analysts cited growing concerns over AI profitability.
items.title: Alphabet's Weak Earnings Trigger Tech Sell-Off

items.summary: President Lee Jae Myung announced during his annual budget speech that South Korea will spend 21.3 trillion won ($16 billion) on chipmaking and artificial intelligence in 2027, nearly double this year's amount, to build a smart military force.
items.title: South Korea Doubles AI and Chip Spending in 2027

items.summary: The 17th meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity concluded in Yerevan, Armenia, after negotiators agreed its main decisions, including the Yerevan Pathway aimed at accelerating global biodiversity action. Held halfway between the adoption and 2030 deadline of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, whose review warned that targets would not be met without faster implementation, the pathway focuses on strengthening efforts to meet existing commitments rather than setting new ones. Nearly $2 billion in new funding was announced by the Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity, alongside a report finding developed countries had failed to provide at least $20 billion annually as promised for 2025. Officials said the next four years will determine whether governments can turn commitments into measurable progress before the deadline. As Schomaker put it: "Ultimately, the test is not what governments agreed in Yerevan, but what they change when they return home."
items.title: COP17 Concludes With Yerevan Pathway for Biodiversity Action

items.summary: Robert Hux, Canadian Director of Schiller Institute, praised China's governance achievements, highlighting poverty eradication and rural infrastructure development. He made the comments following the conclusion of the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China, which set out plans to further strengthen full and rigorous Party self-governance.
items.title: Schiller Institute's Robert Hux Praises China Governance Gains

items.summary: Professional bodies representing counsellors and psychotherapists are calling for statutory regulation in the UK to protect the public from abuse, according to a report hailed as a watershed moment. Unlike doctors or midwives, these titles are not protected nor regulated, allowing anyone to practise without qualification even after misconduct. The Commission for the Future of Counselling and Psychotherapy launched an independent review in October 2025. It estimates about 1.8 million people on waiting lists could fill a treatment gap, with practitioners able to provide more than 370,000 hours of therapy weekly. Campaigner Ella Janneh cited her own case as evidence. Co-chairs Phil Hope and Andrea Sutcliffe argue the government should act given the compelling harm testimony.
items.title: Counsellors and Psychotherapists Urge UK Statutory Regulation

items.summary: A Commons business, innovation, science and trade select committee report concludes the UK is shaping its policy on China “as it goes along” since 2024, risking a strategy dictated by Washington or Beijing. Liam Byrne, Labour MP and chair of the committee, said the piecemeal approach endangers British firms’ EU business and misses opportunities while leaving risks unmanaged. The report cites March’s decision to block Ming Yang from building a £1.5bn wind plant in Scotland as an example of reactivity. It calls for clear new rules, including red and green zones for Chinese investment, amid pressure on the UK to align with EU tariffs on electric vehicles.
items.title: UK MPs Warn Over Ad Hoc China Policy

items.summary: Mitsui Fudosan is pursuing a mixed-use real estate project on land near the British Library, seeking profit from strong London demand while strengthening its brand presence. Kanako Komura, development director at Mitsui Fudosan UK, said the company can leverage expertise in domestic and overseas urban development and large-scale mixed-use projects. The firm cites past redevelopments, including a 52-floor Tokyo Midtown building and a $5 billion Tsukiji site project.
items.title: Mitsui Fudosan Bets on British Library Mixed-Use Project in London

items.summary: Outdoor music events at Tanjong Pagar Distripark have paused after noise complaints from neighbours, organisers said. The Keppel Road venue hosts Ice Cream Sundays by the independent collective Cream Team since 2023; co-founder Jake Camacho was told on Oct 16 that outdoor music could not continue under tighter restrictions. Owner Mapletree posted an Instagram message acknowledging loud music may cause disamenity and asked licensees to pause events, without specifying a duration or names. The group said it had already moved its final Oct 3 event back in the carpark and reduced noise measures. Organisers noted venues are scarce at affordable rates as other sites like Haw Par Villa close after redevelopment; Culture SG's Vira Suria echoed that losing such spaces makes things harder for independent organisers.
items.title: Noise complaints force pause of outdoor music events at Tanjong Pagar Distripark

items.summary: Niklas Persson, CEO of grid integration at Hitachi Energy, tells Euronews Earth that consumers can become “better grid citizens” by using electricity more intelligently rather than simply consuming less. He notes the technology already exists and calls for a partnership between governments, utilities, businesses and consumers to upgrade transmission networks and accelerate permitting. The piece situates this within rising European gas prices expected to stay high into next year, an AI-driven surge in data centres, and smart-meter uptake of 5.9 per cent in Germany — up just 1.5 per cent over six months. Ember cites that smart EV charging could absorb around three per cent of peak wind and solar generation in Spain, where about 10 per cent of monthly power was curtailed in May 2026.
items.title: Hitachi Energy CEO Frames Europeans as Active Grid Participants Amid Rising Prices

items.summary: With the first Harry Potter film marking its 25th anniversary in November, Rail Europe has selected five real-life locations across the UK where fans can experience filming backdrops. The list includes Platform 9¾ at King’s Cross station in London; Warner Bros. Studio Tour London in Hertfordshire, home to “Hogwarts in the Snow,” running from 14 November 2026 to 17 January 2027; Glenfinnan Viaduct in Scotland; Oxford filming sites such as the Bodleian Library’s Divinity School and Christ Church staircase; Durham cathedral; and Goathland station on North Yorkshire Moors Railway. Trains from London take around 45 minutes to Oxford and about three hours to Durham, with heritage trains running seasonally at some sites.
items.title: Five UK Train Journeys Inspired by Harry Potter

items.summary: The Bishop of Wollongong announced that St Michael's Catholic primary school in Mittagong would amalgamate with St Thomas Aquinas in Bowral and close by 2029, becoming Corpus Christi Catholic Parish Primary School. More than 1,600 people have signed a petition opposing the move, which parents say left them blindsided after they were not consulted. The closure follows an assessment of enrolment trends, demographic data and long-term financial viability; no decision has yet been made on the Mittagong site's future use from 2029. Parents, teachers and union representatives have called for a review of the decision.
items.title: Parents oppose closure of historic Mittagong Catholic primary school

items.summary: A sports coach acquitted of making a child amenable to sexual activity has been barred from working with children. A tribunal heard he sent a teenager more than 140 Facebook messages showing an inappropriate and overly familiar pattern of communication, posing what it called an unacceptable risk of harm to children. The ban was upheld.
items.title: Sports coach banned from working with children after tribunal

items.summary: On Sunday, November 2, 2026, US President Donald Trump held rallies in Iowa and Kansas as Republicans made a final push ahead of Tuesday's midterm elections. In Salina, Kansas, he urged voters to elect Republican House and Senate candidates on November 3rd, promising continued America-first policies if they retain control of Congress. He also endorsed Sen. Roger Marshall and Ty Masterson.
items.title: Trump Holds Final Weekend Rallies Before Midterms

items.summary: Nearly 3,000 migrants have reached El Hierro in Spain’s Canary Islands since early October, according to unattributed reporting. On October 22, more than 400 people arrived on four boats from the African coast, per maritime rescue services. Residents fear pressure on infrastructure and resources, with some citing water costs and perceptions of free assistance for migrants. The situation has entered Spain’s political debate ahead of general elections scheduled for November 29.
items.title: El Hierro residents weigh options amid rising migrant arrivals

items.summary: French prosecutors have launched an attempted murder investigation after petrol bombs were thrown at police during unrest, French media reported. An image of a Paris officer with his leg on fire prompted outrage and follows weeks of protests over the cost of living. The burned gendarme told Le Figaro the device had far greater burning capacity than a standard Molotov cocktail. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez called throwing such a cocktail at police "a murder attempt." On Saturday there were more than 770 arrests, roughly half the previous week's total.
items.title: France Opens Attempted Murder Probe After Petrol Bomb Set Officer Alight

items.summary: Antonio Guterres said he was appalled by the death of Mohammed Ibrahim al-Shami, an OHCHR employee arbitrarily detained by Houthis since June 6, 2024. He is the second UN worker to die in custody after a World Food Program staff member who died on Feb. 11, 2025.
items.title: UN chief condemns death of staff member in Houthi detention in Yemen

items.summary: Lindsay Clancy, accused of murdering her three children in 2023, will return to a Massachusetts court on Monday as defence and prosecution teams weigh whether the case should be retried. Her first trial ended in mistrial after a 12-person jury could not reach unanimity; she has not denied the killings but argues postpartum psychosis, while prosecutors insist they were intentional. Lawyers debate dismissal under Rule 25 or double jeopardy grounds versus pursuing justice for her children. Judge William Sullivan is expected to rule on motions and possibly set trial dates at a November hearing, with defence counsel Kevin Reddington noting he could not go to trial until June 2027 if retried.
items.title: Clancy's lawyers and prosecutors debate a retrial before Massachusetts judge

items.summary: Ahead of the US midterm elections, concern over government corruption has become a rare bipartisan consensus in an otherwise polarised electorate. A record 89% of Americans told Gallup that corruption is widespread, up from 73% in 2024 and higher than any other country except Lebanon, Peru, Ghana and Nigeria. In a Fox News Poll, worry about corruption (88%) edged out inflation (85%) and gas prices (83%). Distrust cuts across party lines: the Brennan Center for Justice found negative views toward Congress, Trump, Biden and the Supreme Court alike, with roughly two-thirds seeing it as embedded in institutions. Yet trust in local government remains high at 64%, unchanged since Gallup began polling over half a century ago. Candidates from both parties are leaning on anti-establishment messaging, though analysts say whether this translates into backlash is unclear (s40).
items.title: Americans See Corruption as Top Election Issue Amid Deep Distrust

items.summary: The Trump administration set a November 29 deadline for concluding a trade probe launched in May over alleged intellectual property violations, designating Vietnam as the first priority foreign country in 13 years. Industry groups accuse Vietnam of unfair practices, piracy and inadequate enforcement. Meanwhile, Vietnam's exports to the US surged 42% through eight months this year versus 2025, making it the largest goods-surplus partner ahead of China and Mexico.
items.title: Tesla and Samsung Back US Tariff Probe Against Vietnam

items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said on the Cheeky Pint podcast that keeping DRAM in personal computers is 'quite terrible,' arguing memory ends up being used 5% of the time versus high cloud utilisation. Elon Musk replied, 'The people deserve to have their RAM too!' The piece then shifts to a broader memory shortage pushing up prices across phones, laptops and consoles.
items.title: Altman Calls Personal RAM a Waste; Musk Fires Back Over Memory Shortage

items.summary: Elon Musk acknowledged that xAI reduced compute for its autonomous agent, Grok Bot, because serving it costs more than subscription revenue recoups. Speaking on X after a subscriber requested an early quota reset, he said the cost of running the tool was unsustainably high relative to revenue and offered no scaling promise or timetable. The admission breaks with rivals who quietly throttle capacity while competitors like OpenAI do likewise; analysts note AI token margins must exceed 100% between 2026 and 2030, and reports cite a growing share of abandoned AI projects.
items.title: Elon Musk Admits Grok Bot Is Unprofitable

items.summary: Amanda Peterson Corio, Google's head of data center energy, told The Information that building data centers in orbit could be as much as 100 times costlier than on the ground. She urged exhausting terrestrial options first and framed space as a long-term experiment rather than an immediate fix for Earth-based power constraints.
items.title: Google Energy Chief Warns Space Data Centers Could Cost Far More

items.summary: The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) launched a WhatsApp service for PF members, but users reported it was not working properly within hours of the rollout. Union Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya introduced the service at EPFO's 74th Foundation Day event in New Delhi on Saturday. The service lets subscribers check their balance and passbook details.
items.title: EPFO WhatsApp Service Draws Complaints on Launch Day

items.summary: EAAA India Alternatives Ltd shares are set to list on the BSE and NSE at a grey market premium of Rs 54 per share, or about 3%, over the upper price band of Rs 1,665. The Rs 1,200 crore IPO was an offer for sale with no fresh equity issuance, so all proceeds go to selling shareholder Edelweiss Securities & Investments Pvt. Overall subscription stood at 5. 51 times, led by QIBs at 13. 80 times. Based on FY26 diluted EPS, the issue carried a P/E of about 40 times versus an industry peer average of 39. 89 times. The company reported total income of Rs 964 crore and PAT of Rs 265 crore in FY26. Axis Capital Ltd. , Jefferies India Pvt. Ltd. , Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors Ltd. and Nuvama Wealth Management Ltd. acted as book-running lead managers, with MUFG Intime India Pvt. Ltd. as registrar.
items.title: EAAA India Alternatives Shares List at Under-1% Premium

items.summary: Three Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) members, including two from Punjab—Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Chetan Singh Jouramajra—took part in a gathering where they chanted 'BJP Zindabad' at the Bharatiya Janata Party's Delhi headquarters. Suspended AAP MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh resigned from the Punjab Assembly, having left the Arvind Kejriwal-led party days earlier and joined BJP on Monday. The move drew criticism from ruling Punjab AAP president Aman Arora, who accused BJP of inducting leaders expelled or departed from other parties (attribution: named).
items.title: Big setback ahead of Punjab polls: AAP MLAs chant 'BJP Zindabad' at Delhi HQ, set to join party

items.summary: Around 2.5 lakh shops across roughly 20 to 25 major markets in Delhi stayed closed on Sunday, with traders claiming losses of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore after the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan disrupted business during peak Diwali shopping. CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said nearly 80% of about three lakh shops remained shut amid traffic restrictions and crowd concerns, while roughly 5,000 vehicles could not carry goods to Old Delhi and Central Delhi markets. He noted the affected markets generate around Rs 10,000-12,000 crore during this season. The Automotive Parts Merchant Association opposed the venue's timing, and Rahul Gandhi urged rally participants to shop from local traders while accusing the BJP of spreading rumours about economic harm.
items.title: Delhi Traders Blame INDIA Bloc Rally for Diwali Business Losses

items.summary: Scroll is launching a report investigating whether Mumbai and Kolkata developers and authorities disclose the risk of sea-level-driven home loss to buyers. Citing the United Nations, it says up to 14 million people could lose homes to rising seas. The team plans to map vulnerable areas and check if coastal development destroyed natural buffers like mangroves.
items.title: Mumbai and Kolkata coastal flooding risk investigation by Scroll

items.summary: An article compares how Western outlets covered two October student movements, one in India led by the satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, and another against education funding cuts in France. It argues coverage diverged: Indian reporting emphasised police action, with headlines citing over 2,000 protesters detained on 10 October, while French coverage centred demonstrators' accounts amid allegations of excessive force. Media experts Pradip K Bagchi and Abhijit Mazumdar suggest Western media bias toward the Global South shapes such framing. The piece notes figures like 400,000 protesters across France were reported without attributing them to a single source.
items.title: Western Media Framed India and France Student Protests Differently

items.summary: The Madras High Court ruled that non-Hindus who refuse to pledge reverence or follow traditional customs cannot enter Agamic temples in Tamil Nadu, saying such entry would compromise the shrines' sanctity. In a public interest litigation filed by K Thangam Venkatesh, the bench comprising Justices G R Swaminathan and P Murugan directed strict enforcement of temple-entry rules without political concession. The court distinguished its inclusive approach from performative displays of faith for vote value, citing examples including Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay's entry after signing an undertaking, while directing authorities to uphold age-old customs.
items.title: Madras HC Bars Non-Hindus With Religious Markers From Agamic Temples

items.summary: NTPC reported second-quarter FY27 revenue from operations of Rs 45,752 crore, up nearly 17% year-on-year. The company also announced a first interim dividend of Rs 3 per share with November 6 set as the record date. Shares rose more than 5% in a week. Jefferies maintained its Buy rating with a target price of Rs 425 and raised FY27 EPS by 1%. Nuvama Institutional Equities kept its Buy call at Rs 400, citing strong power demand. The article carries disclaimers that the writer is not SEBI-registered and views are those of the brokerages.
items.title: NTPC shares climb on Q2 results as Jefferies and Nuvama stay bullish

items.summary: Murasu is the name given by the India Meteorological Department to a cyclonic storm heading toward Andhra Pradesh. The word comes from Tamil and refers to a large traditional war drum used during celebrations, warfare and warning of danger. It follows Cyclone Arnab in the North Indian Ocean naming sequence, which contains 169 names contributed equally by each of 13 participating countries and assigned alphabetically rather than by destination. Names must be short, easy to pronounce and politically neutral. A storm receives its name once sustained winds reach at least 34 knots or about 62 kmph.
items.title: The Tamil drum behind cyclone Murasu's name

items.summary: The Delhi Jal Board plans a ₹149 crore, 8.34-km sewer rising main through the ecologically sensitive Yamuna floodplain to curb recurring sewage overflows from three ageing gravity ducts built in 1938, 1972 and 1992. The pipeline has received administrative approval of its estimated cost of ₹148.90 crore, with bids invited on October 26 for a project valued at approximately ₹140.04 crore over 1.5 years. Yamuna activist Bhim Singh Rawat warns that construction in encroached floodplains harms the river ecosystem long-term.
items.title: DJB Approves Yamuna Floodplain Sewer Line Amid Environmental Concerns

items.summary: Nearly 7,000 people attended a free marriage registration camp at the Harahara Mahadeva Temple in Karanthur, near Kozhikode, on November 1, far exceeding organisers' expectations. The queue stretched across two bus stops along the National Highway, prompting police to manage crowds and traffic. Organisers had arranged only 1,500 forms but printed thousands more as demand surged within hours. Press Trust of India reported that about 80 per cent of registrants were men, with many women seeking second marriages; participants said it offered hope after years of unsuccessful searches.
items.title: Kerala Temple Marriage Camp Draws Record Crowd of 7,000

items.summary: Heavy rainfall from Cyclone Murasu affected northern Tamil Nadu as the severe cyclonic storm approached the coast of Tamil Nadu and South Andhra Pradesh. Chennai Airport cancelled at least 11 flights on Monday due to adverse weather conditions, including routes between Chennai-Vijayawada, Rajahmundry, Kadapa and Tiruchirappalli. Greater Chennai Corporation commissioner Sameeran reported no major incidents despite widespread rainfall.
items.title: Cyclone Murasu Cancellations and Rainfall in Tamil Nadu

items.summary: In Andhra Pradesh, police shot a 21-year-old man on Sunday as he allegedly tried to escape custody after attacking a Class 10 schoolgirl with a chainsaw. Several officers were injured; the girl was moved 200 km to Bengaluru for treatment. Separately, Uttar Pradesh Police fired at another suspect in Mathura who opened fire during an anti-murder search operation.
items.title: Police Shoot Two Suspects While Allegedly Fleeing Custody in India

items.summary: A statement by Bengaluru Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh on October 2 gave a fresh twist to the alleged sting operation targeting former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah, bringing Union minister HD Kumaraswamy’s Delhi residence into the investigation. Accused Ritesh Pandey reportedly confessed that a mobile phone used in the operation was bought in Karol Bagh and handed over to Prajwal Prasad at Kumaraswamy’s official residence. The video surfaced on September 27, alleging sexual abuse linked to an incident in 2011. While the disclosure has put Kumaraswamy in a politically uncomfortable position amid his own allegations against Shivakumar, police caution that responsibility cannot yet be fixed and warn against drawing conclusions before digital evidence is verified (s34). The final answer remains awaited as investigators examine financial transactions and CCTV footage (s42-43).
items.title: Probe trail reaches Kumaraswamy’s Delhi home in Siddaramaiah sting case

items.summary: Protesters clashed with security forces in Kangpokpi district after mutilated bodies of two missing youths were found stuffed in gunny bags on a banana farm in Senapati. Police fired tear gas and baton-charged the agitators, injuring one protester whose condition is stable. Deputy Chief Ministers Nemcha Kipgen and Losii Dikho condemned the killings and demanded investigation. Over 50 people have been killed since February clashes between Kuki and Naga communities, while earlier Meitei-Kuki violence claimed over 300 lives. Tribal groups seek an impartial probe into the deaths.
items.title: Protests Erupt in Manipur After Two Missing Kuki Youths Found Dead

items.summary: India's total coal imports declined by 5.83 per cent in August 2026, falling to 104.57 million tonnes from 111.05 million tonnes a year earlier. Imports for blending at domestic coal-based power plants dropped sharply by 35.23 per cent. Union Coal Minister G Kishan Reddy said the decline reflects efforts to boost domestic production and strengthen supply chains, reinforcing energy security.
items.title: India's coal imports fell 5.83% in August, minister says

items.summary: A temple committee's marriage-matching camp drew far more people than expected, with queues spilling across two bus stops along the National Highway and police called to manage traffic. Organisers had planned for 1,500 to 2,000 attendees but saw crowds arrive by 7 am, prompting early form distribution that ran into the evening. Nearly 80 per cent of registrants were men, many above 30, while some women sought second marriages. The committee said it would share an applicant list over about 10 to 20 days and hold future camps every Sunday from 7 am to 10 am starting after November 22.
items.title: Temple Marriage Camp Draws Thousands in Kerala

items.summary: Four Indian brokerage analysts outline technical views as the Nifty index tests resistance at 23,200 after breaking above 22,800 and forming a higher bottom near 22,400. HDFC Securities suggests long positions on dips toward support, while TradeBulls notes improving momentum but flags caution since the index remains below its declining 50-day EMA near 23,170. Anand Rathi requires a decisive breakout above 23,200 plus broader market strength for a sustainable recovery, with immediate support at 22,600 and 22,400.
items.title: Analysts See Nifty's Next Move Hinging on Breakout Above 23,200

items.summary: BJP Union Minister Kiren Rijiju accused the Congress of using an improperly made AI-generated image to depict a large crowd at the INDIA bloc's Sunday rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, which protested against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The allegation was posted on X without a specific image and has not yet received an official response from Congress.
items.title: Congress and BJP Clash Over AI Crowd Image at Ramlila Rally

items.summary: Delhi launched its winter pollution enforcement drive on November 1, inspecting nearly 15,000 vehicles and turning back 1,539 at city borders. Authorities issued 566 challans for PUCC violations worth Rs 56.6 lakh, plus Rs 2 lakh and Rs 9.8 lakh in other penalties, totaling Rs 68.4 lakh on the first day. Traffic police reported a marginal staff shortage amid an INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan; Pankaj Rana said they sent back around six vehicles in five hours and suggested commuters use the metro. Residents like Unis Saifi took Ubers to avoid restrictions, while offices moved to 50% work-from-home until January 31, 2027.
items.title: Delhi's Winter Pollution Drive Fines Drivers, Turns Back Thousands of Vehicles
